traceability.evidence: Implementation exists in src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts, which reads referenced story files, extracts requirement IDs via regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g, caches them per resolvedStoryPath (Map<string, Set>), validates @req IDs against this set, and reports specific ESLint messages reqMissing ("Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'") and invalidPath ("Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'"). Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts are explicitly tagged for docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md and cover: valid existing requirement in a real story (REQ-DEEP-PARSE), valid bullet-list requirement via tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md (REQ-DEEP-BULLET), missing requirement (expects messageId=reqMissing with reqId and storyPath), and invalid paths (traversal and absolute, expecting messageId=invalidPath). The bullet fixture tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md shows requirements in bullet format, which are successfully matched by the regex. Jest aggregated results in .voder/jest-results.json show the suite "Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)" with all tests passing. The rule is integrated into the plugin via src/index.ts: RULE_NAMES includes "valid-req-reference" and TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/valid-req-reference" to "error", so it participates in the recommended/strict configs. User-facing documentation is provided in docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md, which describes deep requirement validation behavior, the error messages, and examples of correct and incorrect usage, and references story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION. The story file docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md defines requirements REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, and REQ-DEEP-ERROR, all of which are implemented or addressed in the rule and its messages (parsing, matching, bullet/ID formats, section-agnostic scanning of entire markdown, caching, and specific error diagnostics). Error handling for unreadable/malformed story files is present via try/catch in loadAndCacheRequirements, which avoids crashes by caching an empty Set and letting reqMissing surface the problem via lint diagnostics.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied: (1) Core functionality: @req annotations are checked against actual REQ- IDs parsed from the referenced story files, with failing tests demonstrating missing requirements are reported. (2) Quality standards: the implementation is format-agnostic to markdown structure and supports multiple requirement formats (plain IDs in text and bullet-list entries) via a generic REQ-… token regex; tests cover at least inline and bullet formats. (3) Integration: the rule is wired into the plugin’s dynamic rule loader and severity map, and coexists with existing annotation-format and story-reference rules. (4) User experience: clear, specific error messages for missing requirements and invalid story paths are defined and asserted in tests. (5) Error handling: file read/parsing issues are caught without throwing, defaulting to an empty requirement set so linting continues and surfaces missing requirements rather than crashing. (6) Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md documents deep requirement validation behavior, supported patterns, and error cases with concrete examples. Therefore this story is fully implemented and passes.
